rounds.text: SC Agrotech Ltd is dramatically under-appreciated by the market, trading at a P/E of just 19.8x [E1] despite exhibiting explosive, hyper-growth across its top and bottom lines. Compounded sales growth has reached 893% over 3 years and a staggering 5,684% over the trailing twelve months, dwarfing the sector median sales growth of 13.0% [E16, E17, E62]. This incredible expansion is translating directly into profitability, with compounded profit growth hitting 94% over 3 years and 64,300% in the trailing twelve months, heavily outstripping the sector median profit growth of 16.1% [E20, E21, E61]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model explicitly points to an intrinsic value of Rs 70 per share compared to the current market price of ₹ 33.5, leaving a massive margin of safety of 51.9% [E42, E43]. The company is virtually debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of -0.00x, and a reverse DCF demonstrates that today's price implies only 7.9% earnings growth against the 18.0% base-case assumption, meaning the market is drastically underestimating the company's trajectory [E37, E44, E48]. Operating margins have also surged dramatically, jumping 118 percentage points over three years to 14% in the TTM and reaching 34% in the June 2026 quarter [E30, E31]. Conceded: promoters hold 0.00% as of September 2026 down from 39.43% in December 2023, and operating cash flow was negative at Rs -107 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E40].

The most alarming signal for SC Agrotech Ltd is the complete abandonment of the business by its insiders, with promoter holding dropping from 39.43% in December 2023 to precisely 0.00% by September 2026 [E40]. This desertion occurs alongside severe cash burn, evidenced by a staggering operating and free cash flow of minus 107 crore rupees in March 2026, leading to a catastrophic cash conversion ratio of -35.67x against reported profits [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, despite reported profits, the company refuses to reward shareholders with any payout, yielding 0.00% on dividends [E4, E50]. Profitability metrics also fail to justify the valuation, as historical returns are persistently weak with a 10-year median return on equity of just 2% and a recent 3-year low ROE of 2.76% [E26, E51], vastly underperforming the sector benchmark of 8.42% [E9]. Additionally, working capital management is deeply strained, plagued by high debtors stretching across 225 days [E52], while operating margins remain inconsistent over the last two years [E32]. Conceded: [E14], [E15], [E16], [E17], [E18], [E19], [E20], [E21], [E30], [E31], [E42], [E43], [E54], [E55], [E56], [E57].

The bear points to promoter exit [E40], but fails to acknowledge that results score a perfect 100 out of 100 while sentiment lags behind, making this a classic turnaround scenario where stale sentiment should not be trusted [E59]. Conceded: [E34], [E35], [E36], [E50], [E52]. The alarming cash burn and debtor metrics are eclipsed by astonishing fundamental acceleration, featuring a trailing twelve month sales growth of 5684% and profit growth of 64300% [E17, E21]. Margins are experiencing a massive structural expansion, with operating margins surging to 14% in the TTM from -104% three years earlier, and reaching 34% in the most recent June quarter [E30, E31]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt free with a debt-to-equity ratio of -0.00x [E37, E48]. Finally, the market price of ₹33.5 significantly underestimates intrinsic value, offering a robust 51.9% margin of safety relative to a DCF value of ₹70 per share [E2, E42, E43].

Conceded: [E17, E21, E30, E31, E42, E43], but these explosive trailing growth figures and margin spikes stand in stark contradiction to the company's deeply troubled structural reality. Conceded: [E59] regarding the sentiment check, yet dismissing a complete promoter wipeout is reckless when insiders holding 39.43% in Dec 2023 have entirely abandoned ship to 0.00% by Sep 2026 [E40]. While the bull celebrates the debt-free status [E37, E48], it glosses over the catastrophic operational failure of a cash conversion reading of -35.67x paired with a massive negative free cash flow and operating cash flow of Rs -107 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, high debtors stretching to 225 days completely undermine the credibility of these reported paper profits [E52]. The low return on equity of 2.76% over the last 3 years and a median ROE of just 2% to 3% across historical periods confirm that capital is deployed with dismal efficiency, regardless of short-term margin fluctuations [E13, E26, E28, E51].
